qualityTarget: Research-grade truth discipline + consumer-grade interaction + premium visual restraint

gates.requirement: Sandbox reuses canonical PublicWorld → World; no parallel ATLAS renderer.
Production branch/domain remain untouched until explicit promotion authority.
New source products enter through a declarative extension registry with domain, role, temporal semantics, source identity, truth boundary and journey hooks.
PLANET/OCE4N/E4RTH/S4PIENS remain domain modes; EARTH/NOW/WATCH remain lenses; question-specific combinations are scenes/presets rather than new ontology.
Every admitted lab layer uses the existing ATLAS ON/OFF machinery.
Raster opacity remains adjustable through the canonical ATLAS layer drawer.
Source authority, product description, checked date and truth caveat are carried with every extension.
Source failure remains explicit and is never rendered or described as zero/no records.
STATIC, SNAPSHOT, TIME_SERIES, CLIMATOLOGY and NEAR_REAL_TIME are kept distinct in extension metadata.
A single ATLAS time control must drive sources that actually expose time without pretending static/climatological layers are live.
Provider-backed legend/class/unit information is required for each promoted lab layer; legacy ATLAS legend metadata is hardened in the sandbox.
Current ATLAS drawer exposes source, caveat and opacity; next pass must expose time basis, coverage/resolution, licence and methodology without turning the interface into a GIS console.
ATLAS context can continue into an existing SPECIES profile while preserving return context.
Living Systems search/context continues to work inside the extended ATLAS runtime.
Before dozens of layers are admitted, the layer console needs search/filter/favourites or progressive grouping so layer count does not become cognitive debt.
Define and test bounds for simultaneous raster/vector sources, tile requests, interaction latency, memory and mobile rendering.
Every accepted release candidate must be browser-proven at desktop 1440 and mobile 390 in the real ATLAS runtime.
Preserve existing keyboard/reduced-motion behaviour and add explicit tests as lab UI grows.
